Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease of apple that commonly affects leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown spots on leaves
Spots may become darker as they develop
Affected leaves may yellow and fall prematurely
Dark or corky lesions may develop on fruit
management: Remove and manage infected fallen leaves
Improve air circulation through appropriate pruning
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease that can affect apple leaves, fruit, and branches.
symptoms: Round leaf spots with darker borders
Brown or dark fruit lesions
Concentric rings may develop in fruit lesions
Fruit may become mummified
Dark cankers may develop on branches
management: Remove mummified fruit and infected plant material
Remove diseased debris from the growing area
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal rust disease that affects apple leaves and sometimes fruit and requires a compatible cedar or juniper host to complete its life cycle.
symptoms: Yellow spots developing on leaves
Orange to orange-red spots
Dark structures may develop within leaf spots
Raised fungal structures may appear on the underside of leaves
Fruit may occasionally develop abnormal lesions
management: Monitor apple trees and nearby cedar or juniper hosts
Remove infected plant material where practical
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Apple___healthy.description: The apple leaf does not show the disease patterns represented by the supported disease classes.
management: Monitor leaves and fruit for changes

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.disease: Cercospora leaf spot / Gray leaf spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal disease of corn that primarily affects leaves and can reduce photosynthetic capacity.
symptoms: Small lesions that develop into elongated rectangular spots
Gray to tan lesions between leaf veins
Lesions may become more numerous as the disease progresses
Severe infection can cause extensive leaf damage
management: Use appropriate crop rotation practices where suitable
Choose resistant or tolerant hybrids where available
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungal disease of corn that produces characteristic rust-colored structures on leaves.
symptoms: Small elongated rust-colored pustules on leaves
Pustules may occur on both sides of leaves
Pustules can release powdery spores
Severe infection may reduce healthy leaf area
management: Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal disease of corn that causes characteristic elongated lesions on leaves.
symptoms: Long gray-green or tan lesions on leaves
Lesions may become cigar-shaped
Lesions can expand and merge
Severe disease can result in substantial leaf damage
management: Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: The corn leaf does not show the disease patterns represented by the supported disease classes.
management: Manage weeds and crop residue appropriately

Grape___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease of grape that can affect leaves, shoots, and fruit.
symptoms: Small yellowish or tan leaf spots
Spots may develop dark margins
Black fruiting structures may develop within lesions
Infected berries may turn brown and then black
Affected berries may become shriveled or mummified
management: Remove infected fruit and plant debris
Remove severely affected plant material where appropriate
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A grape disease complex associated with fungal infection that can affect leaves, shoots, and fruit.
symptoms: Interveinal leaf discoloration
Leaf areas may develop yellow or brown patterns
Small dark spots may appear on berries
Fruit may develop a measles-like appearance
Affected vines may show decline
management: Remove severely affected plant material where appropriate
Follow locally appropriate vineyard disease-management practices

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A fungal leaf disease of grape that causes spots and can lead to leaf damage.
symptoms: Dark spots on grape leaves
Spots may enlarge over time
Affected tissue may become brown or necrotic
Severe infection can result in premature leaf loss
management: Remove severely affected leaves where practical
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness where possible
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Grape___healthy.description: The grape leaf does not show the disease patterns represented by the supported disease classes.
management: Monitor leaves and fruit for changes

Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease of potato that primarily affects foliage and can reduce plant vigor.
symptoms: Dark lesions on leaves
Concentric ring patterns may appear within lesions
Yellowing around lesions
Premature leaf loss in severe cases
management: Provide adequate spacing and air circulation
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Potato___Late_blight.description: A serious disease of potato that can rapidly damage leaves and other plant tissues under favorable environmental conditions.
symptoms: Large irregular dark leaf lesions
Water-soaked appearance may occur under wet conditions
Lesions can rapidly expand
Severe infection can cause rapid plant decline
management: Remove severely infected material where practical
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness where possible
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Potato___healthy.description: The potato leaf does not show the disease patterns represented by the supported disease classes.
management: Keep the growing area free of diseased plant debris

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that can affect tomato leaves, stems, and fruit.
symptoms: Small dark spots on leaves
Spots may have yellow halos
Leaf tissue may become damaged as spots increase
Small dark lesions may develop on fruit
management: Remove severely affected plant material where practical
Avoid working with plants when foliage is wet
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease that commonly affects tomato foliage and can cause progressive leaf damage.
symptoms: Dark brown spots on older leaves
Concentric ring patterns may develop within spots
Yellowing around affected areas
Progressive leaf damage and defoliation
management: Maintain good spacing and air circulation
Keep the growing area free of infected plant debris
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A serious disease that can rapidly damage tomato foliage and fruit under favorable conditions.
symptoms: Dark irregular lesions on leaves
Water-soaked appearance may occur
Lesions can expand rapidly
Severe infection can cause extensive foliage damage
Fruit may develop dark lesions
management: Remove severely infected material where practical
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease that primarily affects tomato leaves, especially under humid conditions.
symptoms: Yellow spots on the upper surface of leaves
Olive-green to brown areas may develop
Velvety fungal growth may appear on the underside of leaves
Severe infection can cause leaf yellowing and drop
management: Remove severely affected leaves where practical
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal disease that commonly causes numerous small spots on tomato leaves.
symptoms: Small circular spots on leaves
Spots may have dark margins
Light-colored centers may develop
Tiny dark structures may appear within spots
Severe infection can cause leaf drop
management: Remove severely affected leaves where practical
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: A pest problem caused by tiny spider mites that feed on plant tissue and can damage tomato leaves.
symptoms: Fine pale stippling on leaves
Yellowing or bronzing of foliage
Leaves may become dry or damaged under severe infestation
Fine webbing may be visible in heavy infestations
management: Monitor the underside of leaves regularly
Remove heavily infested plant material where practical
Reduce plant stress and maintain appropriate growing conditions
Use suitable pest-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease that produces circular lesions on tomato leaves and can affect other plant parts.
symptoms: Circular brown leaf spots
Concentric rings may create a target-like appearance
Spots may enlarge and merge
Severe infection can cause leaf loss
management: Remove severely affected plant material where practical
Use appropriate disease-control products according to their label when necessary

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A viral disease of tomato that can cause characteristic leaf curling, yellowing, and reduced plant growth.
symptoms: Upward curling of leaves
Yellowing of leaf margins or younger leaves
Reduced leaf size
Stunted plant growth
Reduced fruit production
management: Manage insect vectors such as whiteflies
Remove severely affected plants where appropriate
Control weeds that may harbor insect vectors

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A viral disease that can cause mosaic patterns, leaf distortion, and reduced plant growth in tomato.
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
Leaf distortion
Reduced plant growth
Narrow or malformed leaves may occur
Fruit development may be affected
management: Remove severely affected plants where appropriate
Wash hands and tools after handling infected plants
Avoid spreading plant sap between plants

Tomato___healthy.description: The tomato leaf does not show the disease or pest patterns represented by the supported disease classes.
management: Monitor leaves and fruit for changes
